text:
sarah: heads-up — bring-up for the new Llama-ish checkout (model v2-candidate) shows a regression on zh/ja/ko -> en translation when we quantize to int8. float16 baseline looks fine. observed BLEU drop ~27.1 -> 22.3 on our zh->en devset and increased <unk> occurrences. :thinking:

raj: can you paste a minimal reproduction and a tokenizer sample? is this tokenization or a kernel/quant issue?

sarah: quick repro steps:
```
# env: runtime v0.3.3, quant config: int8-dynamic-perchannel
wget s3://redwood-evals/multilang/devsets/zh_en_small.tsv
python eval_translate.py --model checkpoints/v2-cand --tokenizer spm_v2 --quant int8 --input zh_en_small.tsv
```

sarah: sample tokenization diff (float16 vs int8 run with same tokenizer weights):
```
# source: zh sentence with embedded hiragana fragment
"今天天气いいね"
# float16 tokenized pieces:
['▁今天', '天气', '▁いい', 'ね']
# int8 tokenized pieces (weird split):
['▁今天', '天气', '▁い', 'い', 'ね']
# result: extra split in the Japanese fragment -> model emits fragmented translation/hallucination
```

mike: hmm that looks like a tokenizer boundary shift. but tokenizer is shared and hasn't changed between runs, right? any differences in preprocessing (NFKC vs NFC)?

sarah: tokenizer artifact only visible after quantization. same tokenizer binary. suspect runtime/kernels alter byte-level normalization or the run-time input pipeline does an extra normalize step when int8 runtime path is used.

yuki: could be the CJK+Hiragana merging logic in the fast-tokenizer extension. I saw a patch in runtime PR 0f4d2 that touched the pre-tokenization glue. I'll bisect.

li: also check zero-width joiner/ZWJ handling — some mixed-script lines depend on invisible joiners. int8 path might trigger a different utf8 slicing codepath.

sarah: i ran a tiny bisect locally:
- runtime v0.3.2 (good) -> BLEU 27.0
- runtime v0.3.3 (bad) -> BLEU 22.3
commit range: 0f4d2..b9a8f

raj: thanks. can you run a token-level diff tool (showing byte offsets) and capture the exact byte sequences passing into the tokenizer for both runs? if they differ then it's definitely a runtime preprocessing bug.

sarah: done — attached inline: first 24 bytes: (good) e4 b8 8a e5 a4 a9 e5 a4 a9 e6 b0 94 e3 81 84 e3 81 84 e3 81 ad
(bad) e4 b8 8a e5 a4 a9 e5 a4 a9 e6 b0 94 e3 81 84 e3 81 ad
(looks identical at a glance but offsets for multi-byte boundaries shifted in one case)

eval-bot: automated eval run finished — zh->en: float16 27.03 BLEU, int8 22.31 BLEU; ja->en: float16 31.2, int8 28.4; ko->en: float16 26.8, int8 24.0. Full logs: https://storage.redwood/evals/1767456789/logs

mike: ok go deeper: run the same input but bypass the fast-tokenizer and use the Python-only tokenizer (no Rust/C extension) for both quant and fp runs. if discrepancy disappears then bug is in the native extension.

yuki: i ran that — python-only tokenizer yields identical pieces across int8/fp. so it's the fast path. i also instrumented the pretokenizer C++ and saw a branch that toggles on a feature-flag ENABLE_SIMD when CPU supports avx512. the int8 runtime enables ENABLE_SIMD for some kernels. looks promising.

li: there was a micro-optimization for grapheme cluster scanning that changed the iteration order. that could split multibyte graphemes differently.

sarah: action items:
- yuki: revert the ENABLE_SIMD grapheme change in a patch and run full devset by EOD (assigned)
- mike: coordinate with infra to pin runtime v0.3.2 for all int8 validation clusters until we have a fix (assigned)
- raj: add a targeted unit test with mixed Han+Hiragana+ZWJ that runs on both C-extension and python paths (assigned)
- sarah: add failing examples to the model eval harness and mark as regression blocker for v2-candidate

raj: also add a quick regression metric to CI: deltaBLEU > 3 triggers revert gate for quantized model rollouts.

eval-bot: created issue redwood/infra#4321 with logs and attached failing examples

yuki: quick note — preliminary patch (revert) drops the int8 lossless token boundary differences locally and int8 BLEU recovers to ~26.9 (still about 0.1 off from fp; might be noise). i'll open a PR in a few hours.

mike: great. once patch lands we should re-run the full multilingual suite (including punctuation-heavy chinese and vertical text sims). also run quant config int8-static and int4-fp fallback to see sensitivity.

sarah: thanks team. tagging @ops for a short deploy pause for int8 cluster until we validate the revert. :thumbsup: 

li: +1 — will hold the push.

raj: keeping this thread as the canonical repo for reproducer and next steps. I'll follow up once CI regression test is in place. :eyes:
